html:
Argentina is the large country of southern South America, stretching from the subtropical north to Tierra del Fuego. It declared independence in 1816.

Under Spain it was part of the Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata, ruled from Buenos Aires. The May Revolution of 1810 set up self-rule there, and a congress at Tucumán declared independence on 9 July 1816. José de San Martín then led an army over the Andes to free Chile and Peru. Decades of civil war between Buenos Aires and the provinces followed, until a constitution was agreed in 1853.

In the years the map shows from 1880, Argentina boomed:

  • The Conquest of the Desert of the late 1870s and 1880s seized the pampas and Patagonia from Native peoples.
  • Millions of immigrants, mostly Italians and Spaniards, arrived to work the land and fill the cities.
  • Beef and wheat exports made it one of the richest countries in the world by the early 1900s, and Buenos Aires gave birth to the tango.

A coup in 1930 began half a century of instability. Juan Perón, elected in 1946 with his wife Eva, built a mass movement of workers that still shapes politics. Coups followed, and the military regime of 1976 to 1983 waged a Dirty War in which thousands of people were "disappeared". Defeat by Britain in the Falklands War of 1982 brought the generals down. The Nunca Más report recorded their crimes. Since 1983 Argentina has stayed a democracy, though it has lived through repeated debt crises, the worst in 2001.
sum: Argentina is the large country of southern South America, stretching from the subtropical north to Tierra del Fuego. It declared independence in 1816.
